rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A connective clause is omitted between the preceding sentence and this one: the boy was born and grew up.
rows.anchor: بين هذه الجملة والتي قبلها محذوف تقديره: فولد له وشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching the age of saʿy means becoming able to accompany his father in work and errands.
rows.anchor: أي بلغ أن يسعى مع أبيه في أشغاله وحوائجه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وابن زيد
rows.claim: They explain saʿy as work, worship, and assistance.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وابن زيد: والسعي هنا: العمل والعبادة والمعونة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He takes saʿy as walking on foot, specifically walking with settled ability.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: السعي على القدم، يريد سعيا متمكنا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He rejects attaching معه to بلغ or to the verbal noun السعي; the question means the boy had reached the age for work and was asked with whom, namely his father, who was especially gentle. He says the boy was thirteen.
rows.anchor: وفيه قال الزمخشري: لا يصح تعلقه ببلغ به بلوغهما معا حد السعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address my son expresses compassionate tenderness.
rows.anchor: قال يا بني: نداء شفقة وترحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's dream was commanded by God, as the son's instruction to do what he was ordered indicates; prophets' dreams are revelation like waking experience.
rows.anchor: أي بأمر من الله، ويدل عليه: افعل ما تؤمر. ورؤيا الأنبياء وحي كاليقظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham consulted his son despite the binding command to learn his response, steady him if distressed, prepare him for the ordeal, and ease the shock of a sudden trial.
rows.anchor: وشاوره بقوله: فانظر ماذا ترى، وإن كان حتما من الله ليعلم ما عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream setting shows prophetic dreams and waking states agree in truth, as with Joseph's dream and the Prophet's vision of entering the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: كرؤيا يوسف عليه السلام، ورؤيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دخول المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said that when the angels announced a forbearing boy, Abraham replied that the boy would then be God's sacrificial offering.
rows.anchor: قيل: إنه حين بشرت الملائكة بغلام حليم قال: هو إذن ذبيح الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A three-night dream sequence explains the names Tarwiyah, ʿArafa, and Sacrifice Day: first he considered the command, then recognized it as divine, then set out to slaughter his son.
rows.anchor: فلما أمسى، رأى مثل ذلك، فعرف أنه من الله، فمن ثم سمي يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ترى with both letters open, from raʾy, meaning what do you think?
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ترى، بفتح التاء والراء

rows.speaker: عبد الله، والأسود بن يزيد، وابن وثاب، وطلحة، والأعمش، ومجاهد، وحمزة، والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use the form meaning what do you show me so I can consider it?
rows.anchor: وعبد الله، والأسود بن يزيد، وابن وثاب، وطلحة، والأعمش، ومجاهد، وحمزة، والكسائي: بضم التاء وكسر الراء

rows.speaker: الضحاك، والأعمش
rows.claim: Their alternative vocalization means what appears to you or is cast into your heart?
rows.anchor: والضحاك، والأعمش أيضا بضم التاء وفتح الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the syntax, انظر is suspended from its complement and ماذا is interrogative; ذا may be a relative pronoun or part of a compound interrogative, with corresponding changes in the clause's case and object structure.
rows.anchor: وانظر معلقة، وماذا استفهام. فإن كانت ذا موصولة بمعنى الذي، فما مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father's my son is tender, while the son's my father is reverential and respectful.
rows.anchor: ولما كان خطاب الأب يا بني، على سبيل الترحم، قال: هو يا أبت، على سبيل التعظيم والتوقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means what you are ordered to do; the passive verb's object pronoun is omitted after حذف the preposition, under the conditions that permit the deletion.
rows.anchor: أي ما تؤمره، حذفه وهو منصوب، وأصله ما تؤمر به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He offers an alternative parsing as an imperative verbal noun annexed to its passive object, noting disagreement over whether such a governing verbal noun can be made passive.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أو أمرك، على إضافة المصدر إلى المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son's promise to be patient expresses forbearance, patience, compliance with God's command, and contentment with it.
rows.anchor: كلام من أوتي الحلم والصبر والامتثال لأمر الله، والرضا بما أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They both submitted to God's command; أسلما is the majority reading, while استسلم and سلم carry the sense of submission.
rows.anchor: فلما أسلما: أي لأمر الله، ويقال: استسلم وسلم بمعناها. وقرأ الجمهور: أسلما

rows.speaker: عبد الله، وعلى، وابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك، وجعفر بن محمد، والأعمش، والثوري
rows.claim: They read سلما, meaning that both entrusted themselves to God's decree and determination; استسلما is also transmitted, making three readings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله، وعلى، وابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك، وجعفر بن محمد، والأعمش، والثوري: سلما

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He parses أسلما transitively: the father surrendered his son and the son surrendered himself; others take it intransitively as yielding to God.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في أسلما: أسلم هذا ابنه، وأسلم هذا نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talla means Abraham laid his son on one side on the ground and faced the task with endurance and firmness.
rows.anchor: وتله للجبين: أي أوقعه على أحد جنبيه في الأرض مباشرا الأمر بصبر وجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The location is identified as the rock at Mina; al-Hasan places it on the rise overlooking Mina Mosque, and al-Dahhak at today's slaughtering place.
rows.anchor: وذلك عند الصخرة التي بمنى وعن الحسن: في الموضع المشرف على مسجد منى

rows.speaker: بعض البصريين
rows.claim: Some Basrans place the omitted response to لما after وتله, estimating that God granted the pair a great reward.
rows.anchor: أي أجزلنا أجرهما، قاله بعض البصريين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari suggests the omitted response follows رؤيا and refers to what happened, beyond description, including their joy and praise of God.
rows.anchor: أي كان ما كان مما تنطبق به الحال ولا يحيط به الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed placement for the omitted response is before وتله: after they submitted and Abraham laid him down.
rows.anchor: أو قبل وتله تقديره: فلما أسلما وتله

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya attributes the omitted response analysis to al-Khalil and Sibawayh and compares it with a line by Imruʾ al-Qays.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهو قول الخليل وسيبويه، وهو عندهم كقول امرئ القيس

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans say the response is the positive clause وناديناه, with the waw treated as extra.
rows.anchor: وقال الكوفيون: الجواب مثبت، وهو: وناديناه على زيادة الواو

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group takes وتله as the response and treats its waw as extra.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هو وتله على زيادة الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies extended details of Abraham and his son's dialogue and actions, but the author says their soundness is known only to God.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزمخشري في قصة إبراهيم وابنه، وما جرى بينهما من الأقوال والأفعال فصولا، الله أعلم بصحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن introduces an explanation, so the statement means you have indeed confirmed the vision.
rows.anchor: وأن مفسرة، أي قد صدقت

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: He reads the clause without أن, as وناديناه قد صدقت.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: وناديناه قد صدقت، بحذف أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صدقت is also read with a light d, and Fayyad reads الرؤيا with kasra and assimilation, emphasizing confirmation of the vision.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: صدقت، بتخفيف الدال. وقرأ فياض: الريا، بكسر الراء والإدغام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says Abraham exerted himself fully, laying his son down and drawing the blade across his throat; God prevented it from cutting, without making Abraham disobedient or negligent.
rows.anchor: بذل وسعه وفعل ما يفعل الذابح من بطحه على شقه وإمرار الشفرة على حلقه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He rejects treating the event as abrogation of the command before its performance or before the time to perform it.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا من ورود النسخ على المأمور به قبل الفعل، ولا قبل أوان الفعل في شيء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: One reading of قد صدقت is that Abraham accepted in his heart that the dream truly came from God and acted accordingly.
rows.anchor: قد صدقت، يحتمل أن يريد بقلبك على معنى: كانت عندك رؤياك صادقة حقا من الله

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Alternatively, Abraham believed inwardly what the dream established in him and fully discharged its practical demand.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد: صدقت بقلبك ما حصل عن الرؤيا في نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to reward the good explains the relief after hardship and the attainment of the desired outcome after despair.
rows.anchor: تعليل لتخويل ما خولهما الله من الفرج بعد الشدة، والظفر بالبغية بعد اليأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to sacrifice the son was a clear test distinguishing the sincere from others, or a plainly severe ordeal with no harder trial.
rows.anchor: أي الاختبار البين الذي يتميز فيه المخلصون وغيرهم، أو المحنة البينة الصعوبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One identification of the ransom is the ram offered by Abel, accepted by God and kept grazing in Paradise until it ransomed Ishmael.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو الكبش الذي قربه هابيل فقبل منه، وكان يرعى في الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، والحسن
rows.claim: They also identify it as a mountain goat sent down to Abraham from Mount Thawr.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا هو والحسن: فدي بوعل أهبط عليه من سرو

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority describe the ransom as a large white, horned ram with a prominent nose.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: كبش أبيض أقرن أقنى، ووصف بالعظم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the ram's greatness by saying it was certainly accepted.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: لأنه متقبل يقينا

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: He says it was great because the sacrifice became an enduring religious practice.
rows.anchor: وقال عمرو بن عبيد: لأنه جرت السنة به، وصار دينا باقيا إلى آخر الدهر

rows.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
rows.claim: He says it was great because it came from God.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن بن الفضل: لأنه كان من عند الله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: He says it was great because it had not come from offspring but by creation.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: لأنه لم يكن عن نسل، بل عن التكوين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وابن جبير
rows.claim: They explain its greatness by saying it was one of the rams of Paradise, where it had grazed for forty autumns.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: وفديناه بذبح عظيم دليل على أن إبراهيم لم يذبح ابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ransom itself proves that Abraham did not slaughter his son, since the boy was redeemed.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: وفديناه بذبح عظيم دليل على أن إبراهيم لم يذبح ابنه، وقد فدي

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group claims the sacrifice occurred and the boy later returned to life; Ibn ʿAtiyya calls this an outright lie.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: وقع الذبح وقام بعد ذلك. قال ابن عطية: وهذا كذب صراح

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says Abraham thought he had completed the sacrifice, then the command was abrogated; they maintain that he drew the blade but it did not cut.
rows.anchor: لم ير إبراهيم في منامه الإمرار بالشفرة فقط، فظن أنه ذبح مجهز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an says only that Abraham laid his son on his forehead; no sound hadith says he drew the blade across his throat.
rows.anchor: والذي دل عليه القرآن أنه تله للجبين فقط، ولم يأت في حديث صحيح أنه أمر الشفرة على حلق ابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Abraham's memory was left among later people was explained earlier in Noah's story; this passage omits إن because it has been mentioned before and after.
rows.anchor: تقدم تفسير نظيره في آخر قصة نوح، قبل قصة إبراهيم هنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وابن عمر، ومعاوية بن أبي سفيان، ومحمد بن كعب القرظي، والشعبي، والحسن، ومجاهد
rows.claim: They identify the earlier forbearing boy and intended sacrifice as Ishmael, taking the announcement of Isaac as a separate glad tiding.
rows.anchor: وأن الغلام الحليم المبشر به إبراهيم هو إسماعيل، وأنه هو الذبيح لا إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report I am the son of the two sacrificed men identifies Ishmael and his father ʿAbd Allah, whom ʿAbd al-Muttalib vowed to sacrifice before redeeming him with one hundred camels.
rows.anchor: أنا ابن الذبيحين، وقول الأعرابي له: يا ابن الذبيحين، فتبسم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long report about revelation to Moses is cited in support of Ishmael; the author also says Ishmael gave his own life in the sacrifice.
rows.anchor: وفيما أوحى الله لموسى في حديث طويل. وأما إسماعيل، فإنه جاد بدم نفسه

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: When asked by him, a Jewish convert said Jews know Ishmael was the sacrifice but envy the Arabs.
rows.anchor: وسأل عمر بن عبد العزيز يهوديا أسلم عن ذلك فقال: أن يهوديا ليعلم، ولكنهم يحسدونكم معشر العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ram's horns were said to have been hung in the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: وكان قرنا الكبش منوطين في الكعبة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Asked by al-Asmaʿi who the sacrifice was, he argues for Ishmael: Isaac was not in Mecca, where the sanctuary and sacrificial place are, and he built the House with Abraham.
rows.anchor: يا أصمعي، أين عزب عنك عقلك؟ ومتى كان إسحاق بمكة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael's patience at the sacrifice explains his praise as patient, while his promise to his father to endure explains his praise as truthful in promise.
rows.anchor: ووصفه تعالى بالصبر في قوله: وإسماعيل وإدريس وذا الكفل كل من الصابرين

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's identification of Ishmael and says the Jews claim Isaac instead, which he rejects.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبري أن ابن عباس قال: الذبيح إسماعيل، ويزعم اليهود أنه إسحاق، وكذبت اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A strong argument for Ishmael is that if Isaac were the sacrifice, God's announcement that Isaac would father Jacob would not be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: ومن أقوى ما يستدل به أن الله تعالى بشر إبراهيم بإسحاق، وولد إسحاق يعقوب

rows.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب، وابن مسعود، وعلي، وعطاء، وعكرمة، وكعب، وعبيد بن عمير، وابن عباس في رواية
rows.claim: These authorities identify Isaac as the intended sacrifice, with Ibn ʿAbbas holding this in another report.
rows.anchor: وذهبت جماعة إلى أن الذبيح هو إسحاق، منهم: العباس بن عبد المطلب، وابن مسعود، وعلي

rows.speaker: عطاء، ومقاتل
rows.claim: They place the sacrifice at Jerusalem; other reports locate it in Syria or the Hijaz, with Isaac arriving there with Abraham on the Buraq.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء ومقاتل: ببيت المقدس وقيل: بالحجاز، جاء مع أبيه على البراق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says the glad tiding of Isaac refers to the announcement of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: والبشارة في قوله: وبشرناه بإسحاق، هي بشارة نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proponents of Isaac connect Abraham's prayer for a son after migrating to Syria, the announcement of a forbearing boy, and the subsequent dream of sacrificing that boy; they also cite Jacob's letter calling Isaac God's sacrifice.
rows.anchor: أخبر تعالى عن خليله إبراهيم حين هاجر إلى الشام بأنه استوهبه ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who identify Isaac say the announcement was of his prophethood, since a combined promise of his birth and prophethood would undermine the test if Abraham knew he would become a prophet.
rows.anchor: ومن جعل الذبيح إسحاق، جعل هذه البشارة بشارة بنبوته، كما ذكرنا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari poses a grammatical problem if Isaac's birth was promised: his prophethood occurred much later, so نبيا cannot describe him as a circumstantial state at the time of the glad tiding.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت: فرق بين هذا وقوله: فادخلوها خالدين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He contrasts prospective eternity in the command to enter Paradise, which can be estimated as a state, with prophethood, which could not exist when Isaac was not yet born.
rows.anchor: فالخلود، وإن لم يكن صفتهم عند دخول الجنة، فتقديرها صفتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammatical difficulty is solved by supplying an omitted noun: Abraham was promised the existence of Isaac as a prophet, so the state depends on his existence rather than the act of announcing.
rows.anchor: لا بد من تقدير مضاف محذوف وذلك قوله: وبشرناه بوجود إسحاق نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الصالحين is a second circumstantial phrase serving as praise, since every prophet must be among the righteous.
rows.anchor: من الصالحين ، حال ثانية، وورودها على سبيل الثناء والتقريظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God bestowed religious and worldly blessings on Abraham and Isaac, including the prophets of the Children of Israel descended from Isaac.
rows.anchor: أفضنا عليهما بركات الدين والدنيا، وبأن أخرجنا أنبياء بني إسرائيل من صلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous and wrongdoer among their descendants warn Jews who rejected Muhammad; a righteous father may have a wicked child without blame or deficiency.
rows.anchor: فيه وعيد لليهود ومن كان من ذريتهما لم يؤمن بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great distress of Moses and Aaron's people included Egyptian enslavement, fear of Pharaoh's army, and then the sea.
rows.anchor: الكرب العظيم: تعبد القبط لهم، ثم خوفهم من جيش فرعون، ثم البحر بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in We made them victorious refers either to Moses, Aaron, and their people, or only to the two prophets, using a plural pronoun to honor them.
rows.anchor: والضمير في ونصرناهم عائد على موسى وهارون وقومهما وقيل: عائد على موسى وهارون فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun هم may function as a separative pronoun, an emphatic element, or an appositive.
rows.anchor: وهم: يجوز أن يكون فصلا وتوكيدا أو بدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear book is the Torah, as in the verse saying that God sent down the Torah with guidance and light.
rows.anchor: والكتاب المستبين: التوراة، كما قال تعالى: إنا أنزلنا التوراة فيها هدى ونور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path means Islam and God's law.
rows.anchor: والصراط المستقيم: هو الإسلام وشرع الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، وقتادة
rows.claim: They identify Elias as Idris; several readers' version naming Idris is treated by the author as interpretive gloss, not the established wording.
rows.anchor: وإلياس، قال ابن مسعود وقتادة: هو إدريس عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He doubts that the attribution of the Idris interpretation to Ibn Masʿud is sound, since transmitted chronology places Idris before Noah.
rows.anchor: لأن إدريس في التاريخ المنقول كان قبل نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that Sura al-Anʿam places Elias among Abraham's or Noah's descendants; another view makes him a descendant of Aaron, and al-Tabari gives his genealogy through Aaron.
rows.anchor: وفي سورة الأنعام ذكر إلياس، وأنه من ذرية إبراهيم، أو من ذرية نوح

rows.speaker: عكرمة، والحسن، والأعرج، وأبو رجاء، وابن عامر، وابن محيصن
rows.claim: They read the name with a joined initial alif; this may join a hamzat al-qaṭʿ or reflect the name Yasa with the article, as in al-Yasaʿ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة، والحسن: بخلاف عنهما والأعرج، وأبو رجاء، وابن عامر، وابن محيصن: بوصل الألف

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's codex has the reading إبليس for the name.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف أبي ومصحفه: وإن إبليس، بهمزة مكسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إدراس is also read, as a dialect form of Idris, comparable to Ibraham for Ibrahim.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: وإن إدراس، لغة في إدريس، كإبراهام في إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الضحاك، والحسن، وابن زيد
rows.claim: They take Baal as the proper name of the idol worshipped by Elias's people.
rows.anchor: أي أتعبدون بعلا، وهو علم لصنم لهم، قاله الضحاك والحسن وابن زيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account describes Baal as a twenty-cubit golden idol with four faces, served by four hundred attendants who were made to act as prophets; the devil spoke false doctrine from inside it.
rows.anchor: وكان من ذهب، طوله عشرون ذراعا، وله أربعة أوجه، فتنوا به وعظموه

rows.speaker: عكرمة، وقتادة
rows.claim: They say Baal means lord in the language of Yemen.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة، وقتادة: البعل: الرب بلغة اليمن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A man called Baal the lord of a house, prompting Ibn ʿAbbas to invoke the verse rhetorically against worshipping Baal.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: الله أكبر، أتدعون بعلا؟

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says Baal was a woman who came to the people with misguidance and whom they followed.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: إن بعلا اسم امرأة أتتهم بضلالة فاتبعوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long-vowel reading بعلاء is also transmitted, and supports the view that the name refers to a woman.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: أتدعون بعلاء، بالمد على وزن حمراء

rows.speaker: الكوفيون، وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: They read Allah and the following two رب phrases in the accusative, parsing them as apposition or explanatory apposition to أحسن.
rows.anchor: قرأ الكوفيون، وزيد بن علي: الله ربكم ورب آبائكم، بالنصب في الثلاثة

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The other canonical readers use nominative, either implying هو before الله or beginning a new sentence with الله ربكم.
rows.anchor: وباقي السبعة بالرفع، أي هو الله أو يكون استئنافا مبتدأ وربكم خبره

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: A transmission from Hamza has accusative when connected and nominative when pausing.
rows.anchor: وروي عن حمزة أنه إذا وصل نصب، وإذا قطع رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied Elias either by rejecting the statement that God is their Lord and their ancestors' Lord, or by rejecting his call to monotheism, abandon the idol, and accept the messengers.
rows.anchor: فكذبوه: أي كذبه قومه، إما في قوله: الله ربكم هذه النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: محضرون means gathered for punishment.
rows.anchor: ومحضرون: مجموعون للعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is connected to the pronoun in they denied, meaning some of Elias's own people were sincere believers; it cannot sensibly modify the punishment clause or be detached from his people.
rows.anchor: استثناء يدل على أن من قومه مخلصين لم يكذبوه، فهو استثناء متصل من ضمير فكذبوه

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي، ونافع، وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read آل ياسين as two words, taking Yasin as the name of Elias or his father; a further view says Yasin is Muhammad's name.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي، ونافع، وابن عامر: على آل ياسين

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The other canonical readers read إل ياسين as a collective designation for Elias and those affiliated with him, including his followers, and greet them together.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة: على إل ياسين، بهمزة مكسورة، أي إلياسين، جمع المنسوبين إلى إلياس معه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues that if the form were a plural it should be marked by the definite article.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لو كانا جمعا، لعرف بالألف واللام

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء، والحسن
rows.claim: They read الياسين with a joined alif as a plural for Elias and his believing people, with the article attached to the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء، والحسن: على الياسين، بوصل الألف على أنه جمع يراد به إلياس وقومه المؤمنون

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He is reported to read سلام على إدراسين, matching the alternative identification of Elias as Idris; other readings name Idris or Iblis in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود، ومن ذكر معه أنه قرأ إدريس: سلام على إدراسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's wife was the old woman left behind, and was an unbeliever, whether her disbelief was concealed or public; their society permitted marriage to idolaters.
rows.anchor: إلا عجوزا: هي امرأة لوط، وكانت كافرة، إما مستترة بالكفر، وإما معلنة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees are Quraysh, whose trade routes to Syria passed by the towns of Lot's people; the verses urge reflection on what befell those who denied messengers.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في وإنكم لقريش، وكانت متاجرهم إلى الشام على مدائن قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah son of Matta was an Israelite.
rows.anchor: يونس بن متى من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says Jonah became a prophet at twenty-eight, called his people to faith, warned them of the announced punishment, and they repented at its first signs, so God turned it away.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه نبىء وهو ابن ثمان وعشرين سنة، بعثه الله إلى قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The retelling includes only part of Jonah's story to clarify what lies between its two tellings.
rows.anchor: وأعدنا طرفا منها ليفيد ما بين الذكرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fled in anger to board the ship and escape his people; fleeing is called slave flight because he was God's servant who left without God's permission.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن الهروب بالإباق، إذ هو عبد الله، خرج فارا من غير إذن من الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud's report says the becalmed crew drew lots three times, Jonah's lot came up, and after seeing a sea creature await him at every side, he realized the event was from God and jumped to it.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود أنه لما أبعدت السفينة في البحر، ويونس فيها، ركدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits events before the ship and before Jonah's prayer in the darkness; combining this telling with the one in al-Anbiya fills the gaps.
rows.anchor: ففي قصة يونس عليه السلام هنا جمل محذوفة مقدرة قبل ذكر فراره إلى الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defeated in the lots are literally those slipped away from the position of winning in the drawing.
rows.anchor: من المغلوبين، وحقيقته من المزلقين عن مقام الظفر في الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مليم is read with an open mīm; although the expected form is ملوم from a wāw-root, this follows the pattern of أليم, as with comparable forms.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: وهو مليم، بفتح الميم، وقياسه ملوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among those who glorify God means remembering and declaring Him holy; the apparent reference is Jonah's prayer in the darkness in al-Anbiya.
rows.anchor: من الذاكرين الله تعالى بالتسبيح والتقديس. والظاهر أنه يريد ما ذكر في قوله في سورة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the glorification was Jonah's utterance Subhan Allah.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: هو قوله سبحان الله

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group identifies Jonah's glorification as voluntary prayer, with its supporting reports continued in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: تسبيحه صلاة التطوع فقال ابن عباس، وقتادة، وأبو العالية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة، وأبو العالية
rows.claim: They say Jonah's prayer in ease benefited him in distress; al-Dahhak similarly urges remembering God in prosperity so He remembers one in hardship.
rows.anchor: صلاته في وقت الرخاء تنفعه في وقت الشدة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the glorification was Jonah's prayer inside the whale.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: تسبيحه: صلاته في بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: One report says Jonah promised the whale he would build a mosque where none had been built before.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه كان يرفع لحم الحوت بيديه يقول: لأبنين لك مسجدا حيث لم يبنه أحد قبلي

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: Another report says the whale traveled with the ship while Jonah praised God, carried him to shore, and released him unharmed; the people then embraced Islam.
rows.anchor: وروي أن الحوت سافر مع السفينة رافعا رأسه ليتنفس ويونس يسبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that Jonah would have remained in the whale until resurrection; Qatada says its belly would have served as his grave until Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله للبث في بطنه إلى يوم البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author declines to repeat the contradictory reports about how long Jonah stayed in the whale.
rows.anchor: وذكر في مدة لبثه في بطن الحوت أقوالا متكاذبة، ضربنا عن ذكرها صفحا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، والسدي
rows.claim: They say Jonah's body became like that of a newborn child.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عاد بدنه كبدن الصبي حين يولد، قاله ابن عباس والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وأبو هريرة، وعمرو بن ميمون
rows.claim: They identify yaktin as a gourd, whose cool shade, soft touch, broad leaves, and repellent effect on flies made it especially suitable for Jonah.
rows.anchor: اليقطين: القرع خاصة، قيل: وهي التي أنبتها الله عليه

rows.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: The cited poem uses يقطينا as evidence for the plant's name.
rows.anchor: وقال أمية بن أبي الصلت: فأنبت يقطينا عليه برحمة

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet liked gourd and called it Jonah's brother's tree.
rows.anchor: وفيما روي: إنك لتحب القرع، قال: أجل، هي شجرة أخي يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another identification is the banana tree, which shaded Jonah with its leaves and branches and fed him its fruit.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي شجرة الموز، تغطى بورقها، واستظل بأغصانها، وأفطر على ثمارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, a tree is a plant with a stem; God may therefore have miraculously grown a stemmed plant that restored Jonah, since gourd leaves are especially useful for peeling skin.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أنبتنا عليه شجرة، في كلام العرب: ما كان على ساق من عود

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say this was Jonah's first mission, before his flight; the story recounts it at the end to emphasize his prophethood, and the people's respite after believing had provoked his flight.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور: رسالته هذه هي الأولى التي أبق بعدها، ذكرها آخر القصص تنبيها على رسالته
